title: Winter storm or ice
summary: Cold, ice and possible multi-day outages. Heat the house safely and stay off the roads.

items.text: Know the terms: a **watch** means heavy snow or ice is possible within a day or two. A **warning** means severe winter conditions have begun or will soon.
Sign up for your community warning system. NOAA Weather Radio and the Emergency Alert System also give alerts.
Stock supplies for several days without power, including medication and pet needs.
Keep extra batteries for radios and flashlights.
Install and test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors with battery backup.
Seal and insulate the home. Learn how to keep pipes from freezing and where the water shutoff valves are.
Keep backup heat sources on hand, and a fire extinguisher within reach.
items.note: Never use a generator, grill or camp stove inside.

items.text: Prepare the car: test the battery, check antifreeze and tires, and keep a full tank of gas.

Car kit: warm bedding, water and food, first aid kit, flashlight, jumper cables, ice scraper, shovel, sand or non-clumping cat litter, paper map, phone charger, hand warmers, cash and extra medication.
Keep insulin where it will not freeze.
Decide whether to go to Gram's before the roads get bad.
Under a winter storm warning, **find shelter right away**.
Stay off the roads unless travel is absolutely necessary. Check 511Virginia.org or call 511 first.
items.note: If you are trapped in your car, stay in it.

items.text: Dress in several loose, warm layers. Mittens are warmer than gloves. Wear a hat and cover your mouth with a scarf.
items.note: Change out of wet clothing often. Limit time outdoors.

items.text: **Never heat the home with a gas stove or oven.** Use generators and grills outdoors only.
items.note: Keep generators dry. Let them cool before refueling.

items.text: Avoid overexertion when shoveling snow. It can trigger a heart attack.
Know hypothermia: a body temperature below 95°F is an emergency.
items.note: Signs: shivering, exhaustion, confusion, drowsiness. Move to a warm room, warm the chest, neck, head and groin first, and keep the person dry and wrapped in blankets.

items.text: Know frostbite: numb, white or grayish-yellow, firm or waxy skin.
items.note: Move to a warm room. Warm with body heat or warm water. Do not massage the area or use a heating pad.

items.text: Bring pets indoors, and keep fresh, unfrozen water available.
Check on elderly or disabled neighbors and relatives.
If the power goes out, follow the Power outage checklist.
Stay at least 30 feet from downed power lines, treat them as live, and report them to the utility.
Let the generator cool before refueling.
If the power was out more than a day, check food and refrigerated medicine.
items.note: Insulin: read the insulin guide first.
